analyses.failure: test_chk_026_srst_pulse_full_overflow — AssertionError at test_async_gray_fifo.py:1211 'CHK-026: no o_overflow pulse after W1 while blocked' (assert 1 == 0). Fails in all 14 runs (base.s1..s5, model_off, syn, cell1/3/4, macro, small, wr_slow, rd_slow).
analyses.spec_says: Spec AsyncGrayFIFO_Design_Specification.md:912 (scenario 2, rule AF-10.7.4-19): "i_rst_n_sw = 0 for one write-clock cycle only. Writes are blocked at once, o_full stays 1, and no overflow pulse follows although i_wr_en = 1 (the blocked access is not an error)." Spec:176 REQ-SRST-017 (AF-3-61): "a blocked write or read shall not raise o_overflow or o_underflow (DEC-028)". Spec:793 (AF-10.7.2-05): "o_overflow, o_underflow | No pulse for an access blocked by the software reset (DEC-028)". Spec:1101 ERR-005 (AF-12-09) and Spec:1495 DEC-028 say the same. Spec:786 defines wr_blk = o_sw_rst_busy OR (i_rst_n_sw = 0). contract.json:874 CHK-026 expected: "o_overflow=1 at every write edge up to and including W1, from the rejects before W1, and 0 at every edge after W1 while blocked."
analyses.rtl_does: rtl/m_vlsit_afifo_wr.sv:158-163 p_ff_overflow: `reg_overflow <= i_wr_en & w_full_n;`. There is no `~w_wr_blk` term. The block signal exists at line 102 (`assign w_wr_blk = reg_sw_rst_busy | ~i_rst_n_sw;`) and is used for acceptance at line 109, but not for the overflow flop. The comment at lines 156-157 says the opposite of what the code does: "A write that is blocked by the software reset is not an error and raises no pulse." The read side does it correctly: rtl/m_vlsit_afifo_rd.sv:154 `reg_underflow <= i_rd_en & ~w_rd_blk & w_empty_n;`. In CHK-026 the FIFO holds DEPTH words with i_rd_en=0, so the raw full compare w_full_n (line 106) stays 1 from W1 until state PTR resets reg_wbin (lines 131-132). The read pointer never moved, so the read-side reset does not change w_rgray_s. With i_wr_en=1 at every edge, reg_overflow is 1 at every edge after W1 while the write side is blocked.
analyses.test_does: test_async_gray_fifo.py:1161-1198: fills DEPTH words (line 1170), then drives i_wr_en=1 with new data at every write edge. i_rst_n_sw=0 is driven only after tick i==4 (line 1195), so one edge W1 samples it low (w1 = n at line 1194). i_rd_en=0 until busy falls (lines 1173-1179). Checks: o_overflow==1 for edges f+1..W1 (lines 1208-1209; this part passes) and o_overflow==0 for edges W1+1..m+1 (lines 1210-1211; this part fails). The expected value is the contract CHK-026 expected text (contract.json:874), which comes from spec:911-912.

candidates.evidence_for: m_vlsit_afifo_wr.sv:162 does not gate with w_wr_blk, so a blocked write while the raw full is 1 gives a pulse. This breaks REQ-SRST-017/DEC-028/ERR-005 (spec:176, 793, 1101, 1495) and the module's own comment at lines 156-157. The read-side twin (m_vlsit_afifo_rd.sv:154) has the gating, which suggests the write side left it out by mistake. The failure shows up in every configuration, because the scenario keeps the FIFO full through the block. The independent SVA CHK-008 (nnc_chk_wr.sv:89-90) also fails on the same RTL behaviour.
candidates.evidence_against: None found. No spec text allows an overflow pulse for a blocked write while full.

candidates.evidence_for: The edge window might be off by one: the check starts at W1+1, which reflects the access sampled at W1. At W1, i_rst_n_sw=0 is already sampled, so that access is blocked too.
candidates.evidence_against: Spec:912 explicitly says no overflow pulse follows the one-cycle low sample. At W1+1 the pulse reflects the access at W1, which is blocked (i_rst_n_sw=0, spec:786 wr_blk), so 0 is correct there. The edges after that are blocked by busy=1. The window W1+1..m+1 matches contract.json:874. The test passes the first half (lines 1208-1209), so its edge indexing is consistent.

candidates.evidence_for: REQ-ERR-001 (spec:158) says overflow is raised when a write is requested while full. During the block, o_full=1 (DEC-027), so a naive reading could say a pulse is due.
candidates.evidence_against: DEC-028, REQ-SRST-017, ERR-005, spec:793 and the scenario 2 waveform text (spec:912) settle it: a blocked access raises no pulse, even with the FIFO full. The spec is consistent and specific here.

analyses.options: Fix RTL (recommended by the evidence): in rtl/m_vlsit_afifo_wr.sv:162, change to `reg_overflow <= i_wr_en & ~w_wr_blk & w_full_n;` to mirror m_vlsit_afifo_rd.sv:154. This also makes the code match its comment at lines 156-157. Fix test: no change is indicated. Clarify spec: not needed, because DEC-028 is explicit. If the designer instead wanted overflow during the block, then DEC-028, REQ-SRST-017, ERR-005, spec:793 and spec:912 would all have to be rewritten, together with CHK-008 and CHK-026/028/031.

analyses.failure: test_chk_028_srst_reassert_in_rel — AssertionError at test_async_gray_fifo.py:1354 'CHK-028: o_overflow must stay 0' (assert 1 == 0). Fails only in small.s1 (PARA_AFIFO_DEPTH=2, see sim_runs/small.s1.log:27).
analyses.spec_says: contract.json:913 CHK-028 expected: "No write is accepted (none of these words is ever read) and o_overflow stays 0." Spec:936 (scenario 3, AF-10.7.4-21): "i_rst_n_sw = 0 again while the write FSM is in REL. Writes stay blocked ...; i_wr_en = 1 is not accepted." Spec:176 REQ-SRST-017 / spec:1495 DEC-028: "A write or read blocked by the software reset raises no o_overflow or o_underflow pulse." Spec:786: wr_blk = o_sw_rst_busy OR (i_rst_n_sw = 0), which also covers the one-cycle busy gap (spec:1028 R8, spec:1051).
analyses.rtl_does: rtl/m_vlsit_afifo_wr.sv:162 `reg_overflow <= i_wr_en & w_full_n;` has no ~w_wr_blk term. w_full_n (line 106) is the raw pointer compare `reg_wgray == (w_rgray_s ^ LPARA_FULL_MSK)`. With DEPTH=2 (PTR_W=2), the likely mechanism in this test is the following (inferred from the code; no waveform is available). Three words are written (the third is rejected), and two are read with i_rd_en=1, so wbin=rbin=2. The read FSM then resets its pointer to 0 first. The write side sees w_rgray_s=00 while reg_wgray is still gray(2)=2'b11, which equals 00^2'b11. w_full_n then becomes 1 during REQ, before PTR resets reg_wbin (lines 131-132). With i_wr_en=1 held, reg_overflow pulses although the write is blocked. In DEPTH=8 configurations, 3 words are 3 entries and the same transient does not match the full pattern, so the test passes there.
analyses.test_does: test_async_gray_fifo.py:1287-1371: DEPTH-agnostic. It writes 3 words (1306-1307) with i_rd_en=1 throughout (1297-1303). i_rst_n_sw is 0 for 20 cycles, 1 for exactly one edge H, then 0 again until busy has dipped and risen, plus 20 cycles, then 1 (1311-1331). i_wr_en=1 with distinct data at every edge (1336-1337). It expects o_overflow==0 for every edge w0+1..m2+1 (1353-1354). This comes from contract CHK-028 expected (contract.json:913) and DEC-028.

candidates.evidence_for: This is the same missing ~w_wr_blk gating as CHK-026 (m_vlsit_afifo_wr.sv:162, compare m_vlsit_afifo_rd.sv:154). Every write in w0+1..m2 is blocked (busy=1 or i_rst_n_sw=0), so any pulse there breaks DEC-028. The failure appears only when the raw full compare can become true during the block. That happens in DEPTH=2, where the read-pointer reset makes the pointers differ by exactly DEPTH. This fits an ungated-overflow bug that depends on the data path, not a test bug. CHK-008 SVA fails 904 times in small.s1.
candidates.evidence_against: The exact failing edge and pointer values are not in the log; the mechanism above is inferred from the RTL.

candidates.evidence_for: With DEPTH=2, the third pre-sequence write (line 1307) is rejected and gives a legitimate overflow pulse. If that pulse landed inside the checked window, the check would be wrong.
candidates.evidence_against: That write happens before `tb.w(0)` (1308) and `tb.idle(nr=LMAX+6)` (1309), many cycles before w0. Its pulse is one cycle wide, so it cannot reach w0+1. The window w0+1..m2+1 only contains outputs caused by accesses sampled at w0..m2. At w0, i_wr_en was 0 after idle, and from w0+1 the writes are blocked by the input or by busy. So a 1 there is a blocked-access pulse.

candidates.evidence_for: The spec does not separately describe the DEPTH=2 transient in which the raw full compare is true during the handshake.
candidates.evidence_against: DEC-028 covers any blocked access regardless of the internal full state, and o_full is forced to 1 anyway (DEC-027). No clarification is needed to decide that overflow must be 0.

analyses.options: Fix RTL: same change as for CHK-026. Make rtl/m_vlsit_afifo_wr.sv:162 `reg_overflow <= i_wr_en & ~w_wr_blk & w_full_n;`. After the fix, rerun small.s1 to confirm that CHK-028 passes. If it still fails, collect a waveform of reg_wgray/w_rgray_s/state around the failing edge. Fix test: none indicated. Clarify spec: optional. A note that overflow is gated by wr_blk independently of the internal full compare (already implied by spec:786/793) could be added for depth-2 configurations.

analyses.failure: test_chk_031_clock_stop_during_srst — AssertionError at test_async_gray_fifo.py:1453: while i_clk_rd is stopped, got (busy, full, overflow) = (1, 1, 1), expected (1, 1, 0). Record: i_wr_en=1, i_rst_n_sw=1, o_sw_rst_busy=1, o_full=1, o_full_thr=0, i_full_thr=2, o_overflow=1. Only small.s1 (DEPTH=2).
analyses.spec_says: contract.json:961 CHK-031 expected: "While i_clk_rd is stopped: o_sw_rst_busy=1, o_full=1, no write is accepted, and o_overflow=0." Spec:176 REQ-SRST-017 / spec:793 / spec:1101 ERR-005 / spec:1495 DEC-028: a write blocked by the software reset raises no o_overflow pulse. Spec:1069: "o_sw_rst_busy = 1 | A software reset is in progress on the write side. Writes are blocked." Rules AF-10.7.5-09 / AF-20.1-06: the handshake waits while a clock is stopped.
analyses.rtl_does: rtl/m_vlsit_afifo_wr.sv:162 `reg_overflow <= i_wr_en & w_full_n;` (no ~w_wr_blk). With DEPTH=2 the test's 3 pre-reset writes plus the W1 write fill the FIFO (wbin - rbin = 2), so w_full_n (line 106) = 1. With i_clk_rd stopped, the read side never resets its pointer and never acknowledges. The write FSM waits in REQ (lines 175-178), reg_wbin is not reset, and w_full_n stays 1. Because i_wr_en=1 at every write edge, reg_overflow=1 at every edge while blocked (busy=1, line 102). In DEPTH=8 configurations, 4 words do not fill the FIFO, w_full_n=0, and the test passes.
analyses.test_does: test_async_gray_fifo.py:1426-1453: tb.init(ft=DEPTH) (1430). Writes 3 words (1439-1440), then one write with sw=0 (W1, 1441) and one with sw=1 (1442), asserts busy=1 (1443), then stops i_clk_rd (1444). It writes with i_wr_en=1 for 60 write cycles (1446-1447) and checks every edge s0..s1 for (busy, full, overflow)==(1,1,0) (1451-1453). The expected value comes from contract CHK-031 (contract.json:961).

candidates.evidence_for: All writes in the window are blocked (o_sw_rst_busy=1 in the failing record), so DEC-028/REQ-SRST-017/ERR-005 require o_overflow=0. The RTL overflow flop (m_vlsit_afifo_wr.sv:162) ignores w_wr_blk, unlike the read side (m_vlsit_afifo_rd.sv:154) and against its own comment (lines 156-157). The DEPTH-dependence matches: the failure occurs only when the FIFO is actually full during the block (DEPTH=2 with 4 writes).
The test writes DEPTH+ words in the DEPTH=2 build without adjusting. The 3rd pre-reset write (1440) is a legitimate overflow before the block.
candidates.evidence_against: That pulse and the one from the W1-1 write would fall before s0. The window s0..s1 starts after busy=1 was observed (1443-1445), so every access feeding it is blocked. The failing record (i=17, busy=1) is well inside the blocked window. A FIFO that is full when the reset is requested is a legal state, and CHK-026 builds it on purpose.

candidates.evidence_for: CHK-031's rules (AF-10.7.5-09, AF-20.1-06) are about clock stop, not overflow. The overflow=0 expectation is carried over from DEC-028.
candidates.evidence_against: DEC-028 is unconditional for blocked accesses, so the expectation is directly supported by the spec text (spec:176, 793, 1101, 1495).

analyses.options: Fix RTL: rtl/m_vlsit_afifo_wr.sv:162 → `reg_overflow <= i_wr_en & ~w_wr_blk & w_full_n;`. This is the same single change that addresses CHK-026, CHK-028 and CHK-008. Fix test: none indicated. Clarify spec: not required. The designer may add a note that DEC-028 also applies when the FIFO was full at the moment of the request.

analyses.failure: Assertion CHK-008 (nnc_chk_wr.sv:89-91): o_overflow at edge n+1 != (i_wr_en && o_full && i_rst_n_sw && !o_sw_rst_busy) at edge n. 5719 fails / 1683315 hits, first fail at 1080855000 ps (base.s1.log:167, during test_chk_017_synthesis_branch_regression, which runs from base.s1.log:96 at 1075112 ns). Fails in all 14 runs (e.g. small.s1: 904, rd_slow: 656).
analyses.spec_says: contract.json:411 CHK-008 behaviour: "... an access sampled while i_rst_n_sw=0 or o_sw_rst_busy=1 never gives a pulse. A write rejected at an edge before the block starts still gives its pulse in the next cycle." Rules: AF-3-40 REQ-ERR-001 (spec:158) "When a write is requested while the FIFO is full, the overflow flag shall be raised ... 1-cycle pulse"; AF-12-01 ERR-001 (spec:1097) "registered, in the cycle after the rejected request"; AF-3-61 REQ-SRST-017 (spec:176) "a blocked write or read shall not raise o_overflow"; AF-10.7.2-05 (spec:793); AF-12-09 ERR-005 (spec:1101); AF-20.2-24 DEC-028 (spec:1495).
analyses.rtl_does: rtl/m_vlsit_afifo_wr.sv:158-163: `reg_overflow <= i_wr_en & w_full_n;`. w_full_n (line 106) is the raw pointer compare, which is not forced by the block. o_full (line 125) = w_wr_blk | w_full_n. So when i_wr_en=1, the block is active (i_rst_n_sw=0 or busy=1), and the raw full compare is 1, the RTL pulses while the property expects 0. The first fails are 5 consecutive edges 10 ns apart (base.s1.log:167-171, 1080855..1080895 ns, write clock 10 ns). This fits a run of blocked writes on a full FIFO during the CHK-017 random software resets. The other direction (a non-blocked write while full) gives w_full_n=1 = o_full, so the RTL agrees with the property there.
analyses.test_does: SVA verif/sva/nnc_chk_wr.sv:89-90: `@(posedge i_clk_wr) disable iff (!i_rst_n_wr) 1'b1 |=> (o_overflow == $past(i_wr_en && o_full && i_rst_n_sw && !o_sw_rst_busy))`. The expected value is derived from contract CHK-008 behaviour (contract.json:411): overflow = the registered (write requested AND full AND not blocked), with the block = !i_rst_n_sw || o_sw_rst_busy per spec:786. The stimulus comes from all tests; the first fail is in CHK-017 random traffic with software resets.

candidates.evidence_for: The RTL formula (m_vlsit_afifo_wr.sv:162) differs from the spec formula only by the missing ~w_wr_blk term. The property's `i_rst_n_sw && !o_sw_rst_busy` is exactly NOT wr_blk (spec:786: wr_blk = o_sw_rst_busy OR i_rst_n_sw=0). The read side has the term (m_vlsit_afifo_rd.sv:154), and the RTL comment (156-157) states the intended gating. The fails occur in every configuration and in bursts of consecutive write edges, which fits blocked writes while full. The three directed tests CHK-026/028/031 fail for the same reason.
candidates.evidence_against: The fail times were not mapped to individual signal values (no waveform). The attribution to blocked writes is inferred, not proven per fail.

candidates.evidence_for: The property uses $past of o_full, a combinational output that also contains wr_blk. A sampling/race issue at the clock edge, e.g. when i_rst_n_sw changes at an edge, could in principle give mismatches.
candidates.evidence_against: The term `i_rst_n_sw && !o_sw_rst_busy` removes the wr_blk part of o_full, so $past(o_full && !blk) = $past(w_full_n && !blk). That is exactly the spec-intended RTL value. No such race is visible: the companion checks of busy/full timing (CHK-009, CHK-010, CHK-012) do not show matching failures at these times in the excerpt (base.s1.log:140-174 shows only CHK-003/013/008). The property follows the contract text word for word.

candidates.evidence_for: REQ-ERR-001 alone ('requested while full') could be read to include the forced full during the block.
candidates.evidence_against: DEC-028/REQ-SRST-017/ERR-005 explicitly exclude blocked accesses, and CHK-008's behaviour text resolves the boundary case: a reject before the block still pulses, an access sampled while blocked never does. The spec is unambiguous.

analyses.options: Fix RTL: rtl/m_vlsit_afifo_wr.sv:162 → `reg_overflow <= i_wr_en & ~w_wr_blk & w_full_n;` (w_wr_blk = reg_sw_rst_busy | ~i_rst_n_sw, line 102). This matches the property term for term and should clear CHK-008 together with CHK-026/028/031. Then rerun all 14 configurations and confirm fails_CHK_008 = 0. Fix test/checker: none indicated; the property follows contract.json:411. Clarify spec: not needed.
